description.purpose: The cycle watchdog of R-AG-1 (GH #1229). It carries no schedule of its own: ./meter keeps one one-shot named `argus-cycle` under a fixed id and re-arms it (`rearm`) `cycle_ms` ahead after every tick that found an enabled goal. When it strikes, ./meter runs the next cycle.
description.use_when: One per argus hive, always. It is not a poll: an argus whose charter has nothing enabled orders nothing, and the hive rests until an event arrives on `in_cycle` -- a cost alert, a DLQ spike, or the parent's own call after it switched a goal on.
description.not_in_scope: No cron, and no judgement -- it strikes once when the moment the meter ordered comes, and nothing else. The cadence is the meter's `cycle_ms`, not a setting of this cell.
description.emits_meaning: A plain strike, schedule_name `argus-cycle`, which is what the hive's edge to ./meter recognises.
description.consumes_meaning: Schedule ops (add/modify/remove by schedule_id) as body.op -- in practice the one `add` with `rearm` that ./meter sends.
examples: a tick at 06:00:00 that finds an enabled goal -> one order for 12:00:00 -> one strike at 12:00:00 -> ./meter runs the cycle and orders 18:00:00
a tick that finds every goal disabled -> its `idle` receipt and no order -> no strike until `in_cycle`
